page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-48 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g4 server family. It is powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture providing 48 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 180.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The server features a single integrated NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU to accelerate graphics and parallel computing workloads.

This configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via attached network storage volumes. Additionally, the instance does not provide any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local NVMe storage and public IPv4 addresses represents a structural tradeoff, requiring external network configurations for persistent storage and public internet connectivity.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-48 balances a high vCPU count with dedicated GPU acceleration, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring hardware-accelerated rendering, 3D modeling, and workstation virtualization. The allocation of a professional-grade GPU alongside 180.0 GB of RAM makes this server type appropriate for graphics-intensive tasks, offline rendering pipelines, and moderately sized machine learning inference workloads that do not require massive local scratch space.
